verdict.rationale: Copilot documents attaching data in Excel, uploading notes in Word, Analyst for data analysis, and connectors that can find and summarize files, including PDFs, from OneDrive and Google Drive. One community comment praises its cross-document retrieval in 365. However, direct PDF upload for analysis and the accuracy of the analysis are not documented or independently verified. Missing for 10: explicit upload-and-analyze support for PDFs and general documents in the Copilot chat, evidence of analysis accuracy, hands-on corroboration of spreadsheet/PDF analysis quality.

support.subject: As a knowledge-worker, I can upload documents, spreadsheets, and PDFs and get accurate analysis of their contents

citations.quote: Turn raw data into clear insights with Copilot in Excel. Detail your task, attach data, and tweak via chat.
Prompt Copilot with the task, add and upload notes, then refine in the chat—all with Copilot in Word.
Go from raw numbers to real insight—use Analyst to help analyze data with ease.
Connectors allow you to link Copilot to other services so you can easily find, summarize, and act on information from these services.
Search by file name or type: “Find Word documents about vacation plans” or “Show me all PDFs.”
Copilot can also run code to complete complex calculations and generate graphs.
the way it can fetch data from across documents in 365 is really good
